sentences.text: Subsequently, the writ petition came to be allowed on 05.12.2017, primarily, on the ground that the physical possession was with the petitioner and there was construction existing prior to the issuance of notification under Section 4 of the 1894 Act.

4. As per the short-reply by way of the affidavit of Land Acquisition Collector, Urban Estates,
Gurugram, filed on behalf of 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:118973-DB respondents No.1 and 4, the petitioner was not recorded as owner of the acquired land in question at the time of issuance of the notification under Section 4 of the 1894 Act.
It is also pleaded that neither the petitioner nor her predecessor-in-interest filed any objections under Section 5-A of the 1894 Act.

The possession of the acquired land in question was taken over by the Land Acquisition Collector,
Urban Estates, Haryana, Gurugram, vide Rapat Roznamcha No.264 dated 16.03.1993 and the total compensation qua the land in question was Rs.9,28,418.55 Ps.

and qua Khasra Nos.99//4/1 (6-2)
and 7/1 (5-2), out of the said amount, a sum of Rs.1,16,052.30 Ps. had been received by

Smt.
Krishan daughter of Jugal Kishore and rest of the amount of compensation had been sent to the Reference Court, Gurugram under Section 30 of the 1894 Act.

The land in question affects planning of 4 plots of 14 Marla Category, 60 meter wide Sector dividing road and School Site in Sector 39,
Gurugram.

The true copy of the layout plan has been annexed with the short-reply as Annexure R-1.
5.

Keeping in view the law laid down by the Constitutional Bench of the Apex Court in Indore Development Authority Vs. Manoharlal & others, (2020) 8 SCC 129, we are of the considered opinion that once the amount of compensation has duly been deposited under Section 30 of the 1894 Act and the petitioner is not recorded as owner in the revenue record, the question of releasing the land in question in her favour does not arise.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The instant writ petition was filed in the year 2015 challenging the notification dated 22.03.1990 (Annexure P-9) issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the 1894 Act')
which culminated into the notification dated 19.03.1991 (Annexure P-10) under 1 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:118973-DB Section 6 of the 1894 Act and which had led to the passing of the Award on 16.03.1993, whereby the land situated in Village Jharsa, Tehsil and District Gurgaon,
Savitri Devi vs State Of Haryana & Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10686160/
1 was sought to be acquired for public purpose, i.e for development and utilization of residential,
commercial, institutional and maintenance of open space for Sectors 38 to 41 at Gurgaon.
Challenge to the acquisition proceedings has also been raised under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the 2013 Act') on the ground of lapsing.
Apart from that, the plea was taken that the petitioner continued in possession and is still in possession of her house constructed on the land in dispute measuring 11 Kanals 04 Marlas (7/224 share equal to 240 square yards).
Subsequently, the writ petition came to be allowed on 05.12.2017, primarily, on the ground that the physical possession was with the petitioner and there was construction existing prior to the issuance of notification under Section 4 of the 1894 Act.
It is also pleaded that neither the petitioner nor her predecessor-in-interest filed any objections under Section 5-A of the 1894 Act.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Keeping in view the law laid down by the Constitutional Bench of the Apex Court in Indore Development Authority Vs. Manoharlal & others, (2020) 8 SCC 129, we are of the considered opinion that once the amount of compensation has duly been deposited under Section 30 of the 1894 Act and the petitioner is not recorded as owner in the revenue record, the question of releasing the land in question in her favour does not arise.
No replication has been filed by the petitioner to the written statement.
opennyai_summary.decision:
As per order dated 20.09.2023, Mr. N.D. Achint, the counsel for the petitioner, has,
unfortunately, expired and the office has reported that the notice issued to the petitioner has not been received back either served or otherwise.
In such circumstances, we have no other option but to dismiss the present petition for want of prosecution.
